answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can use decaying vouching bonds: each agent stakes tokens to vouch for a newcomer, and the bond earns reputation only as the newcomer completes verified work over time, like a climber inching along a ledge where every step is recorded. If the newcomer turns out fake, the voucher bond is slashed and its trust score drops to the vertex of the network suspicion graph, while the fake identity becomes a relic nobody will vouch for again. Mass forgery then costs a fresh bond and a sponsor risking real stake each time, pricing out cheap identity farms.
